title: Three years in the Navy band and the Army band afterward
summary: Dejan served three years and three months in the Navy, then joined an Army band at Camp Plauche; he compares it unfavorably to the Navy band, and tells of the first Christmas Eve party.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: How long were you in the Navy there, Henry?
Well, I was in there for three years and three months. Three years and three months. Right across there. We stayed in boot camp for 16 weeks, but we can't have the rest of the time.
Oh, you were at the Cross River there.
My brother was with the band at the Lakefront with Daryl Poinnell, Willie Humphrey and them people. Yeah.
And then you played in the Navy band? Yeah. Navy band. Yeah.

Well, after the Navy, they was not making a reserve Navy band. I got in the inactive reserve and when the Army was making a band at Spencer, a very good bass player, teaching music in New Iberraighton, I think. Well, he told me, he said, I'm gonna get an Army band here in the band again. He said, with your rating, he said, you'll be way up there. So I said, I think I will. So I got in the Navy, an Army band then, and Army, Melvin C. Bryant, a music teacher at Dillard University, had a charge in the band. Well, I was assistant, I was a master of the Navy band and also an Army band. Had a wonderful time, plenty of good music to read and play, you know. Had some good musicians in that band. Yeah. This boy was playing bassoon with us, teaching music at St. Augustine now on London Avenue. Oh, wow. Yeah. Yeah, very good. Hampton. Oh, yeah. And this boy, very good clarinet player, is teaching at 35 school right now, Harold Batiste. Oh, yeah. Yeah, he was an Army band, a very fine band. Morett was playing trumpet. This little kid that lived on that street was playing with Tommy Ridgerton now. He was playing with a very good band. Very bad. But I don't think none of them was compared to Navy band, man. I mean, a band as a whole. Yeah. I mean, man for man was different, but a band as a whole, no. Well, we had more time to, all right, we had more time to rehearse us. We commissioned ships all through the day. Sometimes we fish and leave that 4.30 and 25 minutes after, for the phone ring. One of the officers, the captain or somebody wants some music for that night. That ain't that. Yeah, that ain't that. Well, it started us off rough. Well, we first hit here, two days before, the day before Christmas Eve. They told us when y'all, when we hit y'all, y'all gone. Whenever they take our 9, they leave, you see. Waiting to get back home. So, the chief told us, he said, well, tomorrow we gotta play a Christmas Eve party. All the people on the base bring in their family, their children and everything, got Christmas free out there. He said, chief, but the band are leaving together here. So, we had to get together to go play that Christmas Eve party. Everybody was, ooh, we gonna have a wonderful band here on this base. I said, Lord, I didn't know what to say, you know, but they enjoyed it. So, well, time went by, everything went on fine. Everything went fine.
